Hong never imagined that one day he would journey so far.
The road north to Hutuo was arduous—he witnessed refugees everywhere, encountered deserters in conflict, and faced threats from mountain bandits.
Along the way, his appearance became disheveled, his green robe soaked, and his luggage lost.
Only the amulet gifted by his junior brothers remained safely tucked by his side.

Yet the thousand-mile trek inadvertently chipped a corner of the jade pendant.
He was annoyed at his own carelessness, thinking to mend it when leisure allowed.
Straightening his attire, he pressed onward,
heading toward another shattered fragment amid the war-torn lands beyond the mountains.
That corner of the world also awaited his mending.
